title: Fugaro run message (tokens/<repo-slug>/<run-id>/messages/NNNN.msg.json)
description: One message a person sent to a run that is going (docs/run-messages/spec.md, reconciliation F12, F13, F25). It lives under tokens/, the one prefix a job account reads and cannot write (D2941), and the object's name carries the number the run reads it by: the run polls 1..20 and treats a missing number as 'none yet', so the name is the identity. A reader outside the binary — the console, the mobile app, `diagnose` — reads this document; adding a property is fine, removing or retyping one bumps `version`. The store refuses a document this schema refuses, and refuses a few things no JSON Schema can see (a text over the cap in bytes rather than code points, a number in the object's name that disagrees with `seq`), so this is the aid a person checks a hand-written object against and internal/runmsg is the authority.

version.description: The message format the sender wrote, which is the highest one it knows. A runner refuses a version above the one it reads rather than guessing at the shape (F25).

seq.description: The number in the object's own name, which must agree with it: a run reads at most 20 messages and never reads a number past that (F12).

sent_at.description: When the object was written, stamped by the store when the caller leaves it zero.

sent_by.description: The sender as it states itself: display only and never a decision, because no per-object writer metadata exists to check a name against and every launcher can write every run's objects under tokens/ (F1, D2940).

flags.description: What the sender asked for beyond the next coder stage: `now` is the agent's next quiet point inside the stage that is running (D2945), `wrap_up` is commit and stop (D2946). The set is closed and the run advertises the ones its runner honours (F25), so a sender never writes a flag the runner would read as ordinary text.

text.description: The person's own words, bounded at 4 KiB (O1, F12). maxLength counts code points where the store's cap counts bytes, so the schema is the looser of the two and never refuses a text the store wrote; the runner redacts, cleans and fences the text before the agent sees it. No copy of it is in the run record, which a run can rewrite (F13).
